content.value_statement: Large engineering plans often become vague task lists with unclear dependencies. This skill turns plans into vertical-slice tickets with blockers, acceptance criteria, and tracker-ready wording.
actual_capabilities: Breaks plans, specs, issues, or conversations into tracer-bullet tickets.
Marks each ticket with the blockers that must finish first.
Guides the user through review before publishing tickets.
Supports local tickets.md output for repositories without a tracker.
Supports tracker issue creation with native blocking links when available.
Provides templates for ticket bodies and issue descriptions.
limitations: Requires the user or environment to provide tracker configuration.
Does not implement the tickets it creates.
Depends on available context for accurate scope and dependencies.
May need user approval to adjust ticket size before publishing.

use_cases.title: Plan Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Convert a feature spec into small tickets that can ship and verify independently.

use_cases.title: Prepare Agent Work Queues
use_cases.description: Create ready-for-agent tickets with clear blockers and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Organize Refactor Programs
use_cases.description: Split wide refactors into expand, migrate, contract, and verification tickets.

prompt_templates.title: Create Tickets From This Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-tickets to turn the plan in this conversation into a small set of vertical-slice tickets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request using existing chat context.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Spec File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-tickets with the spec at docs/feature-plan.md. Draft tickets, blockers, and acceptance criteria before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Break Down an Existing Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-tickets for issue #42. Read the issue context, propose the ticket breakdown, and ask for approval before publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turning an issue into implementation-ready work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Wide Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-tickets to sequence this refactor with expand, migrate, contract, and final verification tickets. Preserve green CI between batches.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for broad codebase changes.

output_examples.input: A checkout redesign needs backend flags, API changes, UI updates, and tests.
output_examples.output: A numbered ticket plan with one setup ticket, several independently testable vertical slices, blocker relationships, and acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: A shared status field must be renamed across many packages.
output_examples.output: An expand-contract sequence with migration batches, dependency ordering, and a final cleanup ticket.

output_examples.input: A team wants local planning output instead of tracker issues.
output_examples.output: A tickets.md-style plan ordered by blockers, with each ticket describing user-visible behavior and verification steps.

best_practices: Provide the source spec, issue, or conversation context before running the skill.
Review the proposed ticket size and blocker graph before publishing.
Keep each ticket focused on behavior that can be verified independently.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to create layer-only tasks such as database-only or UI-only tickets.
Publishing tickets before the user confirms granularity and dependencies.
Embedding brittle implementation details when a behavior-focused description is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a set of implementation tickets with blockers, deliverables, and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Can it publish to issue trackers?
faq.answer: Yes, when the environment has tracker configuration. It can also write a local tickets.md file.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It plans the work and can hand off individual tickets to implementation workflows.

faq.question: How does it handle dependencies?
faq.answer: It lists which tickets block each ticket and orders publication so blockers come first.

faq.question: Can it handle large refactors?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends expand-contract sequencing and migration batches for broad refactors.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
